facts.raw_span: A 74-year-old Caucasian woman
chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis
treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution
grade 4 neutropenia (<500/μL) for over 15 days
febrile peak
tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs
lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core
severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with minimal necrosis, angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching were seen, along with numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa

concepts.why: The patient developed tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions that progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core, and histopathological examination showed angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, consistent with mucormycosis.
The patient was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia in 2006, with a complex karyotype and TP53 mutation.
The patient developed grade 4 neutropenia, which is a significant decrease in neutrophil count.
The patient was hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis and treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution.
The patient was receiving subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia.
The patient developed grade 4 neutropenia and a febrile peak, which is consistent with febrile neutropenia.
The patient developed skin lesions with features consistent with cutaneous aspergillosis, although the histopathological examination was more suggestive of mucormycosis.
The patient has a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and neutropenia, which suggests an immunocompromised state.

rationales.F03: Complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12 is a high-risk feature for chronic lymphocytic leukemia and immunocompromised state.
rationales.F04: Zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement are treatments for chronic lymphocytic leukemia and hypogammaglobulinemia, indicating an immunocompromised state.
rationales.F07: Grade 4 neutropenia is a strong indicator of neutropenia and febrile neutropenia.
rationales.F11: Severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with angioinvasive microbial structures and hyphal mats is characteristic of cutaneous mucormycosis.
rationales.F12: Thin-walled hyphae with minimal branching and thick-walled ovoid sporangia are characteristic of mucormycosis, ruling out aspergillosis.
